target_customer: AI labs and model developers that train frontier models with reinforcement learning
problem: Training agents with reinforcement learning needs realistic, verifiable environments that labs lack the time to build themselves.
business_model: Custom or catalog RL environments sold to AI labs (pricing not found)
product_category: Reinforcement learning environments and training data

founders.name: Mateo Perez
education: CU Boulder, PhD (research on reinforcement learning and formal methods)

founders.name: Marco
education: University of Stellenbosch, MS (LLMs for test suite generation)
founders.background_notes: YC page does not give a surname or role.

competitors.name: Mechanize
competitors.what: Robust RL environments for AI coding agents sold to labs
competitors.traction_then: Reportedly worked with Anthropic (unconfirmed by the companies)

competitors.name: Prime Intellect
competitors.what: Open Environments Hub for sharing RL environments
competitors.funding_then: Backed by Founders Fund and Menlo Ventures per TechCrunch

technical_complexity.rationale: Building verifiable, non-gameable environments is demanding but uses known tooling; the founders have RL research backgrounds.

defensibility.rationale: Labs build environments in-house and many vendors sell them, so copying was easy and customer lock-in is not documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Data labeling firms added environments, and Mercor agreed to buy Deeptune; no action against Cartpole itself was found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch reported in September 2025 that AI labs were heavily investing in RL environments, and an a16z partner said all big labs were building them in-house, indicating strong demand and spend.

branding.domain_note: Owns cartpole.com per the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: The name likely nods to the classic CartPole RL benchmark, which RL researchers would recognize, but no source states this and generic CartPole results swamp search.

outcome_analysis: Cartpole is a two person Spring 2025 YC company selling RL environments into a market that boomed in 2025 as labs spent on training environments. No traction, customer or round was publicly verified, and no acquisition or shutdown was found, so the outcome is still open and depends on competing with well funded vendors and in-house lab teams.
notes: Funding unverified: Dealroom alone lists a 125K USD seed, not recorded as a round. Team size conflicts (YC says 2, RoundFunded says 1). Competitors come from September 2025 coverage, a few months after the Spring 2025 batch. Company site is a landing page with a contact link only. A single vendor overview claiming Google DeepMind acqui-hired Mechanize was not corroborated and is ignored.
